ming: Heads-up — calliope-v1 int8 bringup showing a weird detok mismatch for vertical CJK output. small BLEU drop on jp-vertical test set (~2.4 -> 1.7). :thinking:

marta: Ugh. Is this at decode time or during tokenization?

ming: Looks like decode/detok. Tokenizer output seems fine (same token ids), but detokenized strings have extra thin spaces and wrong kerning around ruby/annotation markers. Repro snippet:```python
# simplified repro
model = load('calliope-v1-int8')
out = model.generate(prompt)
print(detok(out))
```

samir: Can you paste a before/after example?

ming: Sure. source: "\u6f22\u5b57\uff08\u3075\u308a\u304c\u306a\uff09\n"

calliope-v1-fp16 detok: "\u6f22\u5b57\uff08\u3075\u308a\u304c\u306a\uff09\n"

calliope-v1-int8 detok: "\u6f22\u5b57\n\t\uff08\u3075\u308a\u304c\u306a\uff09\n"

(note: appears as an inserted thin/no-break-ish space and a weird line-kern tag when rendered vertical)

anya: Are those real unicode codepoints or a rendering artifact? Can you hex-dump the bytes?

ming: Hex dump shows U+200A (hair space) and U+202F (narrow no-break space) around the parens only in int8 outputs. fp16 outputs use plain spacing.

marta: That's... surprising. Quant kernel shouldn't add new codepoints. Could be a postprocessing detok path that merges subtokens incorrectly for vertical layout. Any recent changes to detok or locale normalization?

ming: I bisected across the last two weeks of commits. The first bad commit we see is the `detok/vertical-normalizer` change (author: @samir) merged 3 days ago. But int8 only — same commit plus quantized kernels => interaction.

samir: I did touch vertical normalization but only for display mapping (U+200B -> zwsp) not U+202F. Pasting the PR diff:```diff
- map('ZWSP')
+ map('ZWSP', 'THIN_SPACE')
```
That might be too aggressive.

anya: Can we run unit test focusing on ascii/CJK boundary and canonicalize steps for int8 path? Maybe the quantized runtime uses different NFKC/NFKD joins.

ming: Ran quick smoke: `pytest tests/detok/test_vertical_boundaries.py::test_paren_spacing` — fails only on q8 and int8 runtime, passes on fp16 emulation.

qa-bot: New failing test detected (calliope-v1-int8). Link: https://ci.local/runs/90321 :x:

marta: Ok plan: roll back the `THIN_SPACE` mapping in detok and add explicit test cases for narrow spaces. samir, can you revert the one-liner in the PR and push a patch to the detok branch?

samir: On it. I'll push a revert and add a test case. Quick patch:```diff
- normalize_map.update({0x202F: ' '})
+ # leave 0x202F unchanged for vertical render; see issue #4121
```

ming: Also want to capture why quantized kernel path manifests this. I suspect a different whitespace collapse optimization in the int8 token-merge pass. I'll add an instrumentation flag to print token id sequences pre/post merge so we can compare fp16 vs int8.

anya: If we can log token ids + codepoints around the boundary that will help. Maybe the int8 merge uses a heuristic: merge if combined byte length < N; that could break multi-byte unicode sequences.

ming: Added logging to the canary build; pushed to `canary/calliope-int8-detok-log`. CI triggered.

qa-bot: Canary build started for canary/calliope-int8-detok-log (build 90412).

marta: Thanks. Also update the eval harness to measure BLEU at sentence and vertical-render token-level (to catch formatting-only regressions).

samir: Revert PR and patch tests pushed: `detok/revert-thinspace-202F` -> CI green locally. Pushing to origin. :thumbsup:

ming: Canary logs show that int8 merge step was collapsing two subtokens into a single token id that previously stayed separated, and the detok map applied a thin-space substitution on that merged token string. So it's a two-step interaction.

anya: Good find. So we need both the revert and a guard in the merge pass to never introduce codepoints that map to special spacing. Add a rule: if merged surface contains U+202F or U+200A, skip merging.

marta: Sounds right. Add that guard + tests. Also create a short regression eval job to run jp-vertical and cn-vertical testbeds for int8 on every detok change.

ming: I'll schedule a quick rerun of the full evaluation after the guard lands. If BLEU returns to baseline we'll promote int8.

samir: PR: https://git.local/r/1234 updated with guard & tests.

qa-bot: CI passed for detok/revert-thinspace-202F (build 90422). :white_check_mark:

ming: Reran jp-vertical eval on canary int8 after merge: BLEU 2.3 -> 2.4 (baseline 2.45). Close enough for now — running larger job tonight.

anya: Nice. Flagging this for postmortem notes: interaction between normalization and quantized merge passes. Add to eng-ml retro. :eyes:

marta: Agreed. Thanks everyone. Once nightly run is clean we'll onboard calliope-v1 into int8 catalog. :party:

samir: I'll follow up with a tiny doc about why whitespace codepoints are fragile across runtime paths.

ming: Closing thread when nightly results are in. Thanks. :rocket:
